title: Epstein Files Transparency Act
summary: This law requires the Attorney General to publicly release all unclassified Justice Department records relating to Jeffrey Epstein within 30 days, in a searchable and downloadable format. It bars withholding anything to avoid embarrassment, reputational harm, or political sensitivity, while still allowing narrow redactions to protect victims, remove child sexual abuse material, and guard genuinely classified national-security information. The DOJ must justify every redaction in the Federal Register and report to Congress.
brief: Requires the Attorney General to publicly release all unclassified DOJ records relating to Jeffrey Epstein within 30 days, in searchable form, with only narrowly defined redactions allowed.

top_lines.headline: Mandatory Document Release
subs: AG must release all unclassified Epstein-related DOJ, FBI, and U.S. Attorney records within 30 days
Must be published in a searchable and downloadable format
Covers flight logs, immunity and plea deals, detention and death records, and internal DOJ communications

top_lines.headline: Limits on Withholding
subs: No record may be withheld for embarrassment, reputational harm, or political sensitivity
Redactions allowed only for victim privacy, CSAM, active investigations, images of death/abuse, or properly classified material
Every redaction needs written justification published in the Federal Register and sent to Congress

top_lines.headline: Reporting and Named Officials
subs: AG must report to the Judiciary Committees within 15 days of completing the release
Report must list all government officials and politically exposed persons named in the materials, with no redactions

likelihoodReason: Signed into law on November 19, 2025 as Public Law 119-38. The House passed it on November 18 and the Senate on November 19, 2025.

items.main: Names the Act the “Epstein Files Transparency Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Release of Documents Relating to Jeffrey Epstein

items.main: Requires the Attorney General, within 30 days of enactment, to make publicly available in searchable and downloadable format all unclassified DOJ records relating to Jeffrey Epstein.
items.detail: The mandate covers records held by the DOJ, FBI, and U.S. Attorneys' Offices across nine categories, including Epstein's investigations and prosecutions, Ghislaine Maxwell, flight logs and travel records, individuals and government officials named in connection with his activities, entities tied to his trafficking or financial networks, immunity and non-prosecution agreements and sealed settlements, internal DOJ communications about charging decisions, records concerning destruction or concealment of evidence, and documentation of his detention and death including autopsy and medical examiner files.

items.main: Bars withholding records to protect reputations or for political reasons, while permitting narrow, justified redactions.
items.detail: No record may be withheld, delayed, or redacted on the basis of embarrassment, reputational harm, or political sensitivity to any official, public figure, or foreign dignitary. The AG may redact only segregable portions that contain victim personally identifiable information, child sexual abuse material as defined in 18 U.S.C. 2256, material that would jeopardize an active investigation (narrowly tailored and temporary), images of death or abuse, or properly classified national-security information. Every redaction requires a written justification published in the Federal Register and submitted to Congress, and classified covered information must be declassified to the maximum extent possible — with an unclassified summary required where it cannot be.

items.main: Requires the Attorney General to report to the House and Senate Judiciary Committees within 15 days of completing the release.
items.detail: The report must list all categories of records released and withheld, summarize the redactions made and their legal basis, and list all government officials and politically exposed persons named or referenced in the released materials. No redactions are permitted on that list of named officials under the prohibited-grounds rule.

underreported.summary: Any decision to classify covered Epstein-related information after July 1, 2025 must be published in the Federal Register and submitted to Congress, including the date of classification, the identity of the classifying authority, and an unclassified summary of the justification.
underreported.why_unreported: The headline obligation is releasing existing records, but this provision separately governs future classification actions, applying a retroactive cutoff date to constrain classifying covered information rather than disclosing already-held documents.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Comer
featured_quotes.text: as chairman of the House Oversight Committee, I have always believed that sunshine is the best disinfectant. For years, the American people have demanded transparency about Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell's horrific crimes and about the Federal Government's failure to protect the victims. The House Oversight Committee is conducting a thorough review of the Federal Government's investigation into Epstein. Our work goes far beyond the legislation before us today.

gaps: The law requires release within 30 days and reporting after completion but does not specify a consequence or enforcement mechanism if the Attorney General misses the deadline or withholds records improperly.
The law permits temporary withholding to protect active investigations but does not set an outer time limit on how long such material may remain withheld.
The law requires publishing a written justification for each redaction but does not provide a process for the public or Congress to challenge a redaction it considers unjustified.

added: A requirement that the Attorney General publicly release, within 30 days, all unclassified DOJ records relating to Jeffrey Epstein in searchable and downloadable format
A prohibition on withholding records for embarrassment, reputational harm, or political sensitivity
A requirement to publish a written justification in the Federal Register for every redaction and to report named officials and politically exposed persons to the Judiciary Committees
